title: Eocene–Oligocene glaciation
summary: Around 34 million years ago global cooling lasting about 790,000 years shifted Earth from a largely ice-free greenhouse climate to an icehouse, with the first major glaciation of Antarctica. Sediments in Prydz Bay record glaciers advancing into the bay from 34.4 million years ago. A decline in atmospheric carbon dioxide is one of the two leading explanations.

uncertainty.note: Hutchinson et al. (2021) give about 34 Ma lasting about 790 kyr and place the major Antarctic glaciation near 33.7 Ma; Passchier et al. (2017) record glaciers reaching Prydz Bay from 34.4 Ma. Exact steps differ between records.

as_recorded.value: global cooling occurring ∼34 million years ago (Ma) and lasting ∼790 kyr

importance.justification: Marks the start of the modern Antarctic ice sheet and Earth's shift from greenhouse to icehouse.
